summary.text: 果 is a pictograph of fruit growing on a tree. Its common meanings include “fruit” and “result,” though their historical connection is not fully traced.

formation.text: Pictographic: early forms are interpreted as a tree bearing fruit. A curated oracle-style form illustrates this picture; it is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact image.

components.text: 木 is the tree in the depicted scene, while the forms above it represent fruit. The fruit shapes later came to resemble 田; this is not evidence of scribal corruption. 木 is pictorial here, not a sound element or an ancestor of the whole graph.

history.text: Early forms are recorded in oracle-bone and bronze script, with later examples in Chu texts, small seal, and regular script. The described early forms show fruit above 木; later bronze fruit shapes resemble 田, a shape continued in seal and regular script. The available descriptions do not provide a complete sequence of individual forms.

An older analysis identified the oracle form as an early graph for 葉. A later paleographic account disputes that identification through comparison with other plant graphs and 采; the disagreement is not resolved here.

uncertainties.text: Early graphic forms support the pictorial analysis, but do not by themselves prove that a particular inscription used 果 to mean “fruit.” The earliest securely dated fruit context remains unsettled.
Accounts differ on reported early uses: 果然 and a place name, or a proposed use meaning “can.” Their readings and relations to the fruit word remain unsettled.

senses.text: Fruit is identified as the graph’s original meaning in the pictographic analysis and historical dictionary account. Early forms are reported, but a securely dated inscriptional context for this word meaning is not established.
Classical textual citations show uses meaning “result” or “accomplishment.” They do not show when or through what steps these meanings developed from “fruit.”
Dictionary citations document uses such as 果敢, “brave and decisive.” The timing and development of this sense are unresolved.

An account reports oracle-bone use in 果然 and proposes a development from the fruit sense; another discusses early adverbial use. The examples do not establish a dated path or settle the relation to the fruit word.

developments.text: A proposed extension from “fruit” to 果然 remains uncertain because the dates and contexts needed to confirm it are not established.

limitations.text: Historical citations support several uses but do not establish a full chronology or semantic chain among them.
The reported place-name and “can” uses are not connected to the fruit sense by demonstrated semantic development or a supported sound comparison.
